statement.excerpt: The smug, condescending army of AI boosters exists to make you look away from the harsh truth — AI makes very little revenue, lacks tangible productivity benefits, and seems to, at scale, actively harm the productivity and efficacy of the workers that are being forced to use it.
statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

from_speaker: workers that are being forced to use it
our_interpretation: In context, AI means commercial generative AI.
For this ongoing observation, use October through December 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter before the post. This reporting interval is an evaluator choice.
'Lacks tangible productivity benefits' means no meaningful measured improvement in useful work, rather than merely no proven economy-wide transformation.
'Very little revenue' supplies no company perimeter, accounting basis or comparison baseline.
The harm component is tentative and specifically concerns large-scale compelled use; it should not be strengthened into a universal claim.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable revenue evidence establishes a small amount against a defensible stated baseline, while representative workplace measurements show no material productivity benefits and evidence of harm under large-scale compelled use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched-period evidence of meaningful workplace gains contradicts the no-benefits component. Revenue requires a specified perimeter and comparison baseline; evidence of voluntary use alone does not settle the compelled-use component.

evidence.explanation: The experiment ended in November 2025 and found gains on a workplace-style task. Its pooled September-November results and simulated setting do not directly measure the specified quarter or large-scale compulsory workplace adoption.

The follow-up began in August 2025, but its authors identify selection and measurement problems. It neither establishes a reliable fourth-quarter effect nor supports extending the earlier slowdown result to all current users.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined revenue perimeter, accounting basis and comparison baseline, plus matched-period workplace evidence measuring useful output and quality under large-scale required AI use.
